summary:
I looked at 23 apps with a large Gen Z audience. They don't share one winning colour, so "the most successful colour scheme" turns out to be a layout pattern rather than a hue. The most common hue family, red, pink or coral, covers only 7 of 23 apps. What repeats is this: a black-and-white base, one bright, saturated signature colour kept for the brand and the main buttons, greyscale everywhere else, and a dark theme as the default or as an option. 17 of the 19 colour-led brands use a strong, saturated accent, 15 of those 19 accents show up better on black than on white, and 17 of the 19 apps whose theme I could check ship a dark theme. Gradients are rare (3 of 23). This is correlation, not cause. Fi Money used a teal accent and still shut down its banking service in March 2026.

For Vaultwise I recommend a dark-first palette: near-black backgrounds with a lilac-violet signature called "Vault Violet" (#B688FE). Light mode uses a deeper version (#7A36D0). Violet doesn't clash with the four status colours (green, amber, red, blue), and only one of the 23 apps uses it as its main colour. All 123 colour-contrast checks pass WCAG 2.2. The status and category colours are tuned for red-green colour blindness, but the six vault categories still need an icon and a label on screen, because colour alone can't tell them apart for colour-blind users.

findings.claim: No single hue dominates successful Gen Z apps. Across 23 apps, the signature hue families are: red/pink/coral 7, green/lime 4, blue/indigo 4, black-and-white only 4, and teal, orange, yellow and violet 1 each.
findings.evidence: Signature hex values were assigned to hue families by OKLCH hue in analyze-dataset.mjs. The largest family covers only 30% of the 23 apps. In the 12 finance apps the spread is wider still: blue 3, red/pink 3, green 2, teal 1, orange 1, violet 1, black-and-white only 1.

findings.claim: The pattern that repeats is structural: a black/white/neutral base, one bright, high-chroma signature accent used sparingly, and greyscale for everything else.
findings.evidence: 17 of 19 colour-led signatures have OKLCH chroma of at least 0.15 (median 0.214). 15 of 19 have higher contrast on black than on white, so they are built to stand out on dark. Robinhood's 2024 identity is officially black, white and neutrals with occasional Robin Neon (#CCFF00). Opal's official kit is pure black plus gradients that appear only at milestones. Spotify's official logo rules allow the green logo only on black or white.

findings.claim: Almost every app in the set offers a dark theme, and dark-only or dark-by-default apps cluster in media, habit apps and premium or trading fintech.
findings.evidence: Of the 19 apps whose theme I could check, 17 ship dark: 6 are dark-only or dark by default and 11 offer light and dark. Only Venmo and Klarna look light-first, and for those two I couldn't confirm whether a dark mode exists. Spotify still has no light mode (the request is marked Not Right Now). Opal users are still asking for a light theme. Revolut offers Light, Dark or System. Robinhood offers light, dark, market hours or system.

findings.claim: In a July 2026 audit of 520 product design systems, 71% of mobile ones defaulted to dark. Finance was split almost evenly (48% dark, n=42) and entertainment was about 90% dark.
findings.evidence: Lazyweb Research, published 2026-07-07: 267 of 520 systems (51.3%) default to dark, mobile 71% dark, web 68% light. In the finance sample, 22 of 42 are light and 20 of 42 are dark. The authors call the finance sample directional.

findings.claim: Young users strongly prefer dark mode, but the hard numbers come from self-selected or small samples, and none of them isolates Gen Z rigorously.
findings.evidence: In an Android Authority reader poll from 2026 (about 3,100 votes), roughly three in four keep dark mode always on. Its 2020 poll found 81.9% used dark mode wherever available. A 2026 study of 215 users with a mean age of 24.3 found about 68% prefer dark, and the authors call that directional. YPulse (June 2026) reports brands adding dark mode because Gen Z asks for it, but gives no figures. The widely repeated '73% of Gen Z (Adobe)' figure could not be traced to a primary source.

findings.claim: People with normal vision read slightly better in light mode (dark text on a light background), especially small text, so a dark-first app should still offer a light theme and show long documents on light 'paper' surfaces.
findings.evidence: Nielsen Norman Group (2020) summarises Piepenbrock et al. (2013): light mode was better for both younger (18–33) and older adults, and the advantage grows as font size shrinks. NN/g recommends letting users choose dark mode rather than forcing it on a general audience. A 2023 University of Turku thesis found people choose dark mode for a mix of looks and perceived comfort.

findings.claim: Fintech brands lean heavily on blue and purple, red is discouraged for money products, and muted colours tend to earn more trust than very bright ones.
findings.evidence: BFA Global (2021) cites a 2020 analysis of the top 250 finance companies: banks mostly use red, fintechs mostly purple or blue. It ties blue to trust and recommends avoiding red. A study of 1,995 respondents found dull colours were trusted more than bright ones on banking and insurance sites. A pilot study of 225 people on a mobile app found blue earned similar trust whether light or dark. Labrecque and Milne (JAMS) link hue, saturation and value to brand personality.

findings.claim: WCAG 2.2 thresholds: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (18pt, or 14pt bold), and 3:1 for UI component boundaries, states, focus indicators and meaningful graphics. Ratios are not rounded, and the luminance formula uses 0.04045.
findings.evidence: From W3C Understanding SC 1.4.3 and SC 1.4.11. Both are implemented in colorlib.mjs.

findings.claim: About 1 in 12 men have a colour-vision deficiency, mostly red-green, so the usual green-up / red-down money colours must never be the only cue. A leading Gen Z broker ships an accessible-colours toggle for this.
findings.evidence: The US National Eye Institute (NEI) gives the 1-in-12 figure for men and says red-green is the most common type. Robinhood's in-app Theme settings include an 'Accessible colors' toggle to improve colours for red-green colour blindness. In my simulation (Machado 2009 model), the proposed blue/orange alternative for gains and losses reaches CIEDE2000 colour differences of 56.7 (deuteranopia) and 52.8 (protanopia) in dark mode, against 22.7 and 31.4 for the default green/red.

findings.claim: Red-means-up and green-means-down is a cultural convention (mainland China, Taiwan, Japan), not a universal rule. Hong Kong uses the Western mapping.
findings.evidence: Benzinga explains the red-up convention, and a behavioural-economics summary of the Jiang et al. research finds mainland and Hong Kong Chinese hold opposite implicit associations. None of Vaultwise's 8 markets is red-up by default; I could not verify Singapore's convention.

findings.claim: Violet is the least crowded place for a signature colour once the four status colours are taken: only 1 of 23 apps (Jar) uses it as its main colour, and it is far from every status hue. The trade-off is that several fintechs use blue-violet.
findings.evidence: In the hue-wheel scan (accent-whitespace.mjs), #B688FE is at least 40.8 colour-difference units (CIEDE2000) from success, warning and danger. The nearest brand colours are Opal's gradient-only stop #B39AFF (4.2), Discord #5865F2 (16.4) and Copilot #437CEF (17.1). The light-mode version #7A36D0 is close to Jar #7029CC and to CRED's third-party token #6A35FF. WGSN/Coloro's A/W 26/27 key colours include Fresh Purple. Orchid (hue about 320) had the most clear space (minimum 11.6) and is a viable alternative.

findings.claim: The proposed Vaultwise palette passes all 123 WCAG 2.2 checks in both themes. Under simulated colour blindness, success and danger stay at least 15 colour-difference units apart (CIEDE2000), but the six vault categories can collapse to about 8, so every category needs an icon and a label.
findings.evidence: check-palette.mjs reports 123/123 pass. Success vs danger in dark mode: 70.4 normal vision, 22.7 deuteranopia, 31.4 protanopia, 75.2 tritanopia. In light mode: 60.4, 20.8, 15.4, 59.0. The closest category pairs: dark housing vs custom 8.2 (deuteranopia); light health vs retirement 8.2 (deuteranopia) and emergency vs custom 8.2 (deuteranopia), 8.4 (protanopia). The brand violet and the education blue become nearly identical under deuteranopia (0.5).

findings.claim: The audience evidence confirms these apps reach Gen Z heavily, but colour is not a success predictor.
findings.evidence: Pew (2024 teen data): YouTube about 90%, TikTok 63%, Instagram 61%, Snapchat 55%. Pew (2023 survey, published 2024) for US adults 18–29: Instagram 78%, Snapchat 65%, TikTok 62%. Piper Sandler (fall 2025) teens' favourite app: TikTok 46%, Instagram 31%, Snapchat 14%. Cash App had 5M monthly active teen accounts in June 2025. 59% of Robinhood's customers are Gen Z or millennial (YouGov 2026). Fi Money, a teal-branded neobank aimed at young salaried users, wound down banking in March 2026.

findings.claim: Dark themes should use dark grey surfaces that get lighter as they rise, not flat pure black everywhere, because shadows are hard to see on black.
findings.evidence: Material Components' dark-theme documentation uses dark grey instead of black so shadows stay visible. Raised surfaces get lighter through overlays or tonal surfaces. Third-party summaries of Apple's guidelines describe the same 'base vs elevated' approach; I could not open Apple's own page.

spec:
# Vaultwise mobile colour system: research and spec (2026-10-10)

## 1. The answer, in one paragraph
The most successful Gen Z apps don't share a hue. They share a **structure**:
- a black/white (or near-black) base;
- **one bright, highly saturated signature colour**, kept for the brand and the primary action (Spotify green, Robinhood Robin Neon, Snapchat yellow, TikTok cyan/red, Cash App green);
- greyscale for everything else;
- a dark theme as the default or one tap away;
- gradients only for special moments.

Vaultwise should copy that structure, not someone else's hue. Recommendation: **Vault Black (#0B0A10) + Vault Violet (#B688FE)** as the brand. This is correlational evidence. Colour does not cause success (Fi Money's teal brand did not save its banking service, wound down in March 2026).

**How to read the evidence.** **Fact** means documented by the cited source. **Observed** means read from the company's live website code on 2026-10-10. **Inference** means my reasoning from the data.

---

## 2. Dataset (23 apps)

Source codes: O = official brand page, guideline or help article. S = company's own site code or meta tags observed 2026-10-10. T = third-party colour database (lower confidence).

| YouTube | entertainment | #FF0000 | #212121 | red (29) | system | T | Teens about 90% (Pew) |
| Duolingo | habit | #58CC02 | #1CB0F6, #89E219 | green (138) | system (light default) | O (design.duolingo.com via search) + T | — |

| Cash App | finance | #00D64B (site); #00D632 (T) | #000000 | green (147) | dark surfaces (low confidence) | S + T ([Lazyweb](https://www.lazyweb.com/research/what-theme-do-finance-apps-launch-with.md)) | 5M monthly active teen accounts, June 2025 ([Payments Dive](https://www.paymentsdive.com/news/block-courts-teen-app-users/757214/)) |

| Fi Money | finance | #00B899 | #14CCAD gradient | teal (175) | not verified | S | Banking wound down March 2026 ([TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/03/11/india-neobank-fi-winds-down-banking-services-on-its-platform)) |
| Copilot Money | finance | #1C6CFF | navy #000814 | blue (262) | system (dark supported) | S + T | Apple Design Award finalist 2024 ([App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id1447330651)) |
| Klarna | finance | #FFA8CD | #0B051D, #F9F8F5 | pink (353) | light-first | S + O (Pink badge) | Gen Z BNPL: 54% used it for 2024 holidays ([J.D. Power](https://www.jdpower.com/business/press-releases/2025-us-buy-now-pay-later-satisfaction-study)) |

## 3. Aggregates (computed by `analyze-dataset.mjs`)

**Hue family, all 23 apps:**
- red/pink/coral 7 (30%)
- black-and-white only 4
- blue/indigo 4
- green/lime 4
- teal 1, orange 1, yellow 1, violet 1

**Hue family, 12 finance apps:** blue 3, red/pink 3, green 2, teal 1, orange 1, violet 1, black-and-white only 1.

**Saturated ("neon") accents:** 17 of the 19 colour-led signatures have OKLCH chroma of at least 0.15. The median is 0.214. Only Klarna's pastel pink and Fi's teal are softer.

**Built to stand out on dark (inference):** 15 of 19 signature colours have higher contrast on black than on white. Only Pinterest, Revolut and Jar are below 4.5:1 on black.

**Theme defaults:**
- 11 offer light and dark (follow the phone or let the user choose)
- 6 are dark-only or dark by default
- 2 are light-first
- 4 not verified
- So 17 of the 19 verified apps ship dark.

**Gradients as a core brand element:** 3 of 23 (Instagram; Opal, for milestones only; Fi).

**Wider context:**
- In a July 2026 audit of 520 product design systems, 71% of mobile ones defaulted to dark; finance was split 52% light / 48% dark (n=42); entertainment was about 90% dark ([Lazyweb](https://www.lazyweb.com/research/what-percent-of-apps-default-to-dark-mode.md)).

**The dominant patterns to copy (inference from the above):**
- **P1.** A neutral base plus one saturated signature colour, used sparingly.
- **P2.** Dark surfaces first, with light mode available.
- **P3.** Colour carries meaning (actions, status), not decoration.
- **P4.** Gradients only for celebration moments.

## 4. Evidence that shaped the choices

**Dark-mode preference**
- In Android Authority's 2026 reader poll (about 3,100 votes), roughly 75% keep dark mode always on. Its 2020 poll found 81.9%. Both are self-selected samples.
- A 2026 study of 215 young users (mean age 24.3, recruited in Vietnam) found about 68% prefer dark.
- Nielsen Norman Group (NN/g) / Piepenbrock 2013: light mode reads better for people with normal vision (ages 18–33 and 60–85), especially at small text sizes.
- **Consequence:** dark is the hero theme, but documents (invoices, proofs, terms) appear on light "paper" cards even in dark mode, and a Light option exists.

**Colour and trust in fintech**
- Fintechs cluster in blue and purple; red is discouraged for money brands ([BFA 2021](https://bfaglobal.com/?p=247757)).
- Dull colours were trusted more than bright ones (n=1,995).
- **Consequence:** keep the big surfaces calm and neutral and limit the saturated colour to the accent, which is the Robinhood "neutrals + pops" model.

**WCAG 2.2:** 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text, 3:1 for UI parts and focus indicators ([1.4.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html), [1.4.11](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)). SC 1.4.1 says colour must never be the only cue.

**Colour blindness**
- About 1 in 12 men are affected, mostly red-green ([NEI](https://www.nei.nih.gov/learn-about-eye-health/eye-conditions-and-diseases/color-blindness)).
- Robinhood ships an "Accessible colors" toggle for red-green colour blindness ([help](https://www.robinhood.com/us/en/support/articles/accessibility-options)).
- Red-up is the convention in mainland China, Taiwan and Japan ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/general/education/21/10/23258001/did-you-know-you-dont-want-to-be-in-the-green-if-youre-trading-in-china-japan-or-taiwan)), so always show +/− signs and ▲/▼ arrows.

**Dark surfaces:** use dark grey and step surfaces lighter as they rise, rather than pure black everywhere ([Material](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/material-components/material-components-android/master/docs/theming/Dark.md)).

## 5. Signature colour decision

**Chosen: Vault Violet**
- Dark mode #B688FE (OKLCH 0.72 / 0.17 / 300).
- Light mode #7A36D0 (OKLCH 0.51 / 0.22 / 298).

**Why violet:**
- **(a) No clash with status colours.** Green, amber, red and blue are all reserved for status. Violet sits at least 40.8 colour-difference units (CIEDE2000) from success, warning and danger.
- **(b) Little competition.** Only 1 of 23 apps uses violet as its main colour (Jar, India).
- **(c) It follows the pattern.** It is a bright accent that glows on black: 7.46:1 on the background, with dark text on violet fills.
- **(d) It fits the trends.** It suits current Gen Z colour trends; WGSN/Coloro list Fresh Purple among A/W 26/27 key colours.
- **(e) It replaces the plain blue.** It moves away from the navy/blue the user found plain.

**Risks:**
- Several fintechs use blue-violet (BFA; Revolut #494FDF, Discord #5865F2).
- The light-mode violet #7A36D0 is close to Jar #7029CC.
- I could not verify checkout-button competitors (Shop Pay, Zip).

**Alternative B: "Orchid" (dark #CB82EE, about hue 320).** It had the most clear space in the hue scan, but it reads more playful and less "trust".

**Brand rule**
- The identity is **Vault Violet on Vault Black**, two colours, like Robin Neon on black.
- Logo: a single-colour violet mark, or a white mark on violet.
- Category colours are UI-only and never appear in the logo, app icon or marketing.

## 6. Tokens

### Dark (default / hero theme)
| Token | Hex | Use |
|---|---|---|
| bg | #0B0A10 | Screen background (near-black, slight violet tint) |
| surface | #16151D | Cards, tab bar |
| surfaceRaised | #201E29 | Sheets, modals, pressed cards |
| border | #2E2C3A | Decorative dividers only |
| borderStrong | #6E6A80 | Input outlines, focusable boundaries (≥3:1) |
| text | #F5F4F9 | Primary text, amounts |
| textMuted | #A9A6B9 | Secondary text, captions |
| accent | #B688FE | Primary buttons, active tab, selection, brand |
| accentPressed | #A473EE | Pressed or active state of accent fills |
| onAccent | #0B0A10 | Text and icons on accent fills (dark ink, like Spotify/Robinhood) |
| accentText | #C7A8FD | Links and accent-coloured text |
| accent2 ("Aura", optional) | #7BE3F5 | Gradient partner only (violet→aura) for milestones: goal reached, proof approved, "Pay with Vaultwise" success. Never used for status. |
| success | #52E9B2 | Approved, verified, gains |
| warning / warningFill | #FFCD54 | Pending, hold, near limit (with onWarning #0B0A10) |
| danger | #F0503A | Declined, errors, losses |
| info | #C7A8FD | Same as accentText; info "speaks in the brand voice", which keeps blue free for Education |
| onStatus | #0B0A10 | Text on any status fill |
| *-soft containers | status colour at 12% over surface | success #1D2E2F, warning #322B24, danger #301C20, info #2B2738 |

### Light (full equivalent)
| Token | Hex |
|---|---|
| bg | #F7F6FB |
| surface | #FFFFFF |
| surfaceRaised | #FFFFFF (+ shadow) |
| border | #E3E1EC |
| borderStrong | #8A8699 |
| text | #14121C |
| textMuted | #5D596C |
| accent | #7A36D0 |
| accentPressed | #6824B7 |
| onAccent | #FFFFFF |
| accentText | #742EC9 |
| accent2 | #0E899F |
| success | #047A5C |
| warning text | #895706 |
| warningFill | #F5AF20 (with onWarning #1A1300) |
| danger | #C9241B |
| info | #742EC9 |
| onStatus | #FFFFFF |
| *-soft | status colour at 8% over white: success #EBF4F2, warning #FEF9ED, danger #FBEDED, info #F4EEFB |

**Light-mode warning rule:** show warnings as an amber fill or icon with dark text. Don't use amber-brown text alone, because it is confusable with danger under deuteranopia (5.5 colour-difference units).

### Vault categories (UI-only: icon tint, progress ring, chip, chart series)
| Category | Dark | Light | Hue rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| health | #4DECE4 | #077F7A | aqua / medical teal |
| education | #5FA7FD | #3A81D7 | sky blue |
| housing | #F8A650 | #C06F0A | apricot / clay |
| emergency | #F36069 | #C52D23 | siren red; deliberately shares the danger hue family, so it always shows the siren icon |
| retirement | #D96BB2 | #C34E97 | sunset pink (keeps the web app's pink) |
| custom | #C2F26C | #456B07 | lime (keeps the web app's green) |

**Rules:**
- Category colours never colour money amounts or status.
- Category names use the `text` colour.
- Every category always has an icon and a label.
- In light mode, category colours are never used for text: education (3.96:1) and housing (3.80:1) only pass the 3:1 UI threshold.

### Gains and losses (Invest)
- Default: up = success, down = danger, always with +/− and ▲/▼.
- Add a Settings toggle, "Colour-blind friendly gains/losses":
  - Dark: up #5FA7FD, down #F8A650.
  - Light: up #2F6FD0 (4.88:1), down #B35F00 (4.61:1).
- With the toggle on, the colour difference between gains and losses rises from about 23 to about 57 under deuteranopia.

### Usage proportions (inference from P1)
- Neutrals cover about 85–90% of any screen.
- Accent covers 10% or less: one primary button, the active tab, key highlights.
- Status colours appear only where there is a status.
- Gradients only in milestone moments, never behind amounts or text blocks.

## 7. WCAG 2.2 contrast results (from `check-palette.mjs`, 123/123 pass)

| Pair | Dark | Light | Need |
|---|---|---|---|
| text on bg / surface / raised | 18.02 / 16.56 / 15.00 | 17.24 / 18.53 / 18.53 | 4.5 |
| textMuted on bg / surface / raised | 8.30 / 7.63 / 6.91 | 6.28 / 6.75 / 6.75 | 4.5 |
| accentText on bg / surface / raised | 9.81 / 9.01 / 8.17 | 6.56 / 7.05 / 7.05 | 4.5 |
| accent fill vs bg / surface / raised | 7.46 / 6.85 / 6.21 | 5.98 / 6.43 / 6.43 | 3 |
| onAccent on accent / pressed | 7.46 / 5.88 | 6.43 / 8.32 | 4.5 |
| borderStrong vs bg / surface / raised | 3.79 / 3.48 / 3.16 | 3.28 / 3.53 / 3.53 | 3 |
| border vs surface (decorative) | 1.33 | 1.29 | n/a |
| accent2 vs bg | 13.28 | 3.83 | 3 (decorative) |
| success / warning / danger / info text on surface | 11.78 / 12.18 / 5.10 / 9.01 | 5.33 / 6.12 / 5.60 / 7.05 | 4.5 |

## 8. Colour-blindness separation

Simulation model: Machado 2009, severity 1.0. Distances are CIEDE2000 colour differences. About 20 or more is clearly distinct at a glance; below 10 risks confusion.

| | Dark | Light |
|---|---|---|
| success vs danger: normal / deuteranopia / protanopia / tritanopia | 70.4 / 22.7 / 31.4 / 75.2 | 60.4 / 20.8 / 15.4 / 59.0 |
| closest status pair, deuteranopia | warningFill~danger 18.7 | success~danger 20.8 |
| closest category pair, normal vision | emergency~retirement 20.0 | housing~emergency 24.0 |
| closest category pair, deuteranopia | housing~custom 8.2 | health~retirement 8.2; emergency~custom 8.2 |
| closest category pair, protanopia | education~retirement 14.1 | emergency~custom 8.4 |
| closest category pair, tritanopia | emergency~retirement 8.8 | housing~retirement 8.0 |
| accent vs education, deuteranopia | 0.5 (they look the same) | — |

**Takeaway:** status colours stay apart under every simulated deficiency. Six categories cannot all be told apart by colour alone for red-green deficiencies; this is a physical limit with only one usable hue axis. So icons, labels and position are mandatory. Buttons are already identified by shape and label.
